meta.name: decision-reintroduction-bench-v2
meta.purpose: Downstream behavioral benchmark, rebuilt after adversarial review. Does Decision Memory steer an agent to an empirically-backed choice it would not make on its own?
meta.source_graph: dogfood-code-memory (local CE) — real code decisions mined from kumiho-SDKs history
changes_from_v1: Buckets: only `behavioral` items form the headline. `general_knowledge` (a-priori best practice) and `recall` (internal-state) are reported separately, not as behavioral wins.
Blind judge: the judge sees only bare `right_action`/`wrong_action` (no rationale, no numbers), presented in a deterministically-shuffled order as Option 1/2. Rich fields are for humans only.
Control arm B' (decoy_brief): a plausible generic prior-decision brief with NO decision/number, to separate 'this specific evidence' from 'any in-context authority'.
skip_hub_entities FIXED: v1 rewarded hard-skip, which its own brief supersedes (deferred hub anchors, -0.078). R is now 'defer, do not hard-skip'.
evidence_token: a specific measured token that must appear verbatim for a VERIFIED citation (not just an LLM 'cites=true').
Neutral task phrasing: both options presented symmetrically.
meta.honesty: Selection is non-blind (same author drew the decisions, wrote the options and signals). Behavioral n is small by design — only decisions whose right answer is a non-obvious Kumiho measurement qualify. Effect attributable to memory = (arm B) − (arm B' decoy), not (arm B) − (arm A).

items.why_question: why is the based_on field removed from the summarizer schema?
items.task: You're finalizing the consolidation summarizer's JSON output schema. One option keeps an optional `based_on` provenance field that records which facts each decision drew on; the other omits it entirely. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Omit the `based_on` field from the summarizer schema.
items.wrong_action: Keep the `based_on` provenance field in the summarizer schema.
items.decoy_brief: [D1] Schema design principle: prefer explicit, well-documented fields and capture provenance where it aids traceability and downstream auditing. [D2] Keep serialized consolidation outputs stable across releases and review any schema change for backward compatibility.
items.wrong_option: Keep based_on — richer provenance at no apparent cost.
items.right_option: Remove based_on so the summarizer output stays byte-identical; emitting the field shifts structured output and weakens base recall.
items.evidence_quote: Measured: emitting `based_on` shifted every consolidation's structured output and weakened base recall; removing it recovered fulltext/IDF quality +0.031 (temporal +0.065).

items.why_question: why is the cross-encoder run per sub-query instead of on the merged set?
items.task: For multi-hop recall with several reformulated sub-queries, you can apply the cross-encoder rerank + widen-trim either once on the merged candidate set, or separately per sub-query before merging. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Rerank + widen-trim per sub-query, before merging.
items.wrong_action: Rerank + widen-trim once on the merged candidate set.
items.decoy_brief: [D1] Retrieval principle: cross-encoder reranking improves precision over bi-encoder recall; place it where it most improves final ranking quality. [D2] Keep the recall pipeline simple and maintainable; avoid redundant passes when a single pass suffices.
items.wrong_option: Rerank once on the merged set — simpler, one pass.

items.why_question: why is the additive partition unconditional?
items.task: In compose_context, bridge/fact evidence and conversation memories share one context budget. You can either let all entries compete purely by score, or unconditionally reserve the head of the context for the conversation memories. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Unconditionally reserve the head of the context for conversation memories.
items.wrong_action: Let all entries compete for the budget purely by score.
items.decoy_brief: [D1] Context assembly principle: order retrieved context by relevance so the most pertinent evidence is prominent. [D2] Keep the assembly logic uniform across query types to reduce special-casing.
items.wrong_option: Let everything compete by score; the top-K cut decides.
items.right_option: Partition unconditionally so conversations own the head of the context.
items.evidence_quote: Measured: in LoCoMo-Plus 500-char contexts, typed one-liners led while the answer's own session block trailed and got cut.

items.why_question: why does the sibling reserve ride on top of the cap instead of inside it?
items.task: Kumiho reserves some recall slots for sibling revisions alongside the base + edge payload. You can carve that reserve out inside the fixed context cap, or add it on top of the cap. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Add the sibling reserve on top of the cap (as a strict superset).
items.wrong_action: Carve the sibling reserve out inside the fixed cap.
items.decoy_brief: [D1] Budget principle: keep the assembled context within a fixed token cap and allocate slots to the highest-value evidence. [D2] Avoid unbounded growth of the context; a predictable budget keeps latency and cost stable.
items.wrong_option: Carve the reserve inside the cap (keep the total fixed).
items.right_option: Add the reserve on top of the cap; an in-cap reserve evicted proven edge entries when the base filled.
items.evidence_quote: The old in-cap reserve evicted ALL proven edge entries whenever the base filled, trading proven multi-hop edge payload for unproven siblings.

items.why_question: why is ABOUT removed from the default recall edge types?
items.task: Kumiho can traverse ABOUT edges (memory to entity) during recall. You can keep ABOUT in the default recall edge_types to widen recall, or gate it opt-in. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Gate ABOUT opt-in (remove it from the default recall edge_types).
items.wrong_action: Keep ABOUT in the default recall edge_types.
items.decoy_brief: [D1] Graph recall principle: traversing more edge types can widen recall but also adds noise; choose edge types that contribute genuine, content-bearing signal. [D2] Prefer conservative defaults and let advanced traversal be opt-in.
items.wrong_option: Include ABOUT by default — more edge types widen recall.
items.right_option: Gate ABOUT opt-in; entity anchors are content-less, so the single ABOUT hop dead-ends and injects empty stubs.
items.evidence_quote: Review finding: entity anchors are content-less, so traversing ABOUT injects empty stubs and the single hop dead-ends.

items.why_question: why does the bridge join skip ubiquitous hub entities?
items.task: Kumiho's multi-hop bridge join can be flooded by ubiquitous high-degree 'hub' entities (e.g. the two speakers, linked from nearly every memory). You can hard-skip (drop) hubs above a degree threshold, or defer them so low-degree bridges surface first and hubs only fill any leftover budget. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Defer high-degree hub entities (low-degree bridges first; hubs fill leftover budget), do not drop them.
items.wrong_action: Hard-skip (drop) high-degree hub entities above a threshold.
items.decoy_brief: [D1] Graph retrieval principle: highly-connected 'hub' nodes can dominate traversal and dilute discriminative signal; manage their influence so specific, low-frequency connections remain visible. [D2] Prefer approaches that preserve recall coverage while reducing noise.
items.wrong_option: Hard-skip hubs above a degree threshold (drop them).
items.right_option: Defer hubs (surface discriminative low-degree bridges first; hubs fill leftover budget). Hard-skipping was measured worse.
items.evidence_quote: Hub hard-skip cost multi-hop -0.078; hub anchors are now DEFERRED instead of dropped — low-degree bridges surface first, deferred hubs fill remaining budget.

items.why_question: why is rerank_async a single-worker executor?
items.task: You're wiring a synchronous fastembed cross-encoder reranker into Kumiho's async recall pipeline. You can drive it from a dedicated second event loop, or offload it to a worker thread off the main event loop. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Offload the blocking call to a worker thread / executor off the event loop (no second event loop).
items.wrong_action: Drive the reranker from a dedicated second event loop.
items.wrong_option: Drive it from a dedicated second event loop.
items.right_option: Offload to a worker thread off the event loop; a second event loop corrupts httpx's loop-bound pool.
items.evidence_quote: A second event loop corrupts httpx's loop-bound connection pool; a concurrency-4 harness degraded to ~1 effective concurrency when the rerank blocked the loop.

items.why_question: why does recall deduplication key on query and scope instead of a global timestamp?
items.task: Kumiho suppresses accidental duplicate recall calls within a short window. You can dedup on a single global timestamp per session, or on a signature of the call (query + scope). Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Dedup on a signature of the call (query + scope).
items.wrong_action: Dedup on a single global timestamp per session.
items.right_option: Signature over query + scope so distinct concurrent calls never collide.
items.evidence_quote: Live incident: 4 of 6 concurrent agents got count=0 'Duplicate recall' on their first DISTINCT call under a global timestamp.

items.why_question: why is entity promotion scheduled fire-and-forget instead of awaited inline?
items.task: During consolidate_session, entity promotion writes entity nodes to the graph. You can await it inline (so it completes before the store returns), or schedule it fire-and-forget. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Schedule entity promotion fire-and-forget (do not block the store).
items.wrong_action: Await entity promotion inline before the store returns.
items.right_option: Fire-and-forget; it must not delay the store.
items.evidence_quote: Measured: entity promotion was awaited inline, so every store paid the entity-write cost synchronously.

items.why_question: why is sibling reranking hybrid instead of a pure LLM reranker?
items.task: Kumiho ranks sibling revisions of a memory. You can rank purely with an LLM reranker, or use the LLM with a deterministic in-process fallback. Which do you choose, and why?
items.right_action: Use the LLM reranker with a deterministic in-process fallback.
items.wrong_action: Rank purely with the LLM reranker.
items.right_option: Hybrid with a deterministic fallback so the primary revision survives when the LLM path fails.
items.evidence_quote: Graph node records a hybrid sibling reranker with an env-wired cross-encoder and wide-then-trim recall (a deterministic fallback path).

items.why_question: is KUMIHO_MEMORY_ONTOLOGY default ON or OFF, and why?
items.task: As of the current release, is Kumiho's ontology feature (KUMIHO_MEMORY_ONTOLOGY) shipped default ON or default OFF? Give the current state and the reason.
items.wrong_option: Default OFF / opt-in — conservative for a newer feature.
items.right_option: Default ON (opt-out) after it was measured as a net improvement.
items.evidence_quote: Flipped from default OFF (2026-07-08) to default ON / opt-out (e52e5df1, 2026-07-10) after measuring +0.042 overall, all five LoCoMo categories up.

items.why_question: why must the fact-recall leg run under space-scoped recalls?
items.task: A review suggested skipping the fact-recall leg whenever a recall is already space-scoped, to avoid redundant work. Given how Kumiho's own recall path actually behaves, should you take that suggestion? Give the answer and the reason.
items.right_action: Do not skip; run the leg under space-scoped recalls.
items.wrong_action: Skip the leg when the recall is already space-scoped.
items.wrong_option: Take the suggestion — skip when space-scoped.
items.right_option: Do not skip; the scope-skip is too blunt (space_paths is passed on every recall, so the leg never fires).
items.evidence_quote: The scope-skip was too blunt: the harness passes space_paths on every recall, so the leg never fired (0 firings).
